criteria.rationale: Linux same-machine liveness is established only with host, application-specific machine and boot digests, namespace and process start. Missing context remains unknown. Cooperating writers and process-crash scope are explicit; no power-loss or daemon guarantee is inferred.

Directory flock serializes recoveries and each rechecks owner digest and liveness. Exclusive publication prevents acquisition before removal. Race tests and 20 additional two-recovery/acquisition rounds preserve the new lock and start record; release removes only its own bytes.

The sealed B13 producer traverses Store, CLI and MCP. Whole journal reads and blocked checkpoints propagate typed failures; action_journal_invalid and optional start-status lock fields agree across consumers. Existing quickstart lifecycle remains executable.

Schema, sequence, trailing values, blank lines, unterminated tails, oversize events, duplicate effective keys including nested aliases, and unknown event types are refused. Empty recover-lock and conflicting modes exit 2 before domain effects. Counterfactual regressions fail without the guards.

The current integration producer exercises both CLI renderers and MCP action requests/start status through the shared domain readers. Local scripts, skills, workflows, docs and CI consumers were searched; nine actual journals and the full quickstart remain valid. External Harne8 sources were outside authorized clone scope.

Invalid journals locate exact line, byte offset, length, SHA-256 and valid-event prefix without deriving a partial view. Five checkpoint states and three owner states remain distinct. Independent denied-write probe preserves confirmed results/index effects and records checkpoint uncertainty separately.

New strict refusals and recover-lock are minor changes, documented in ADR and changelog. Existing success documents and exit codes remain; checkpoint, replaced_checkpoint and lock fields are optional. Legacy empty locks remain unknown and require operator inspection.

Full Go tests, vet, race, cross-platform builds, 31 assertion-killed production-only overlays, P01-P17 comparisons, exact line boundaries, unavailable checkpoints and lock races support the reviewed behavior. F1-F4 are resolved; full-surface second-round review found no new blocker.

D1 follows from the fact that editable progress does not prove repository effects: journal reads fail closed and checkpoints never authorize skipped steps. D2 follows from persistent sentinels surviving process death: identity and OS exclusion govern recovery, never age. The ADR bounds nonauthoritative rename durability honestly.

mappings.rationale: The ADR makes journal and checkpoint evidence fail closed for D1 basis R1-R5; its start-owner protocol follows D2 basis R6-R8. No age-based recovery or new authority is introduced.

Unreflected progress conflicts until apply names the current plan. Dead-lock recovery preserves spec and start record, and quickstart apply/wait/attest/resume passes.

R1-R9 and V1-V8 are covered by the sealed integration producer plus independent mutation, fault and concurrency probes. R4 distinguishes nonauthoritative checkpoint durability from repository effects. R8 preserves interrupted start intention without claiming a future runtime was implemented.

The 34 declared artifact paths and four attributed commits implement B13 only, with no policy, capability or adoption changes. agent:independent- is the engine-required declaration until pose-delegated-review-run-provenance replaces it. This maintainer-authorized Codex/OpenAI execution is another vendor than implementer Claude/Anthropic. Identity is declared and pose-dist attestations are unsigned.

No raw machine or boot ID is recorded or published. Strict shared readers reject ambiguous effective fields before views and gates. Recovery requires inspected bytes and a proven-dead owner; live and unknown owners stay protected. Synthetic probes expose no credentials and no authority boundary was weakened.

The change uses one journal parser, a strict checkpoint inspector and a bounded start-owner protocol. A universal publisher, automatic repair or daemon would add authority and coordination beyond B13. B10/B14/B15/B35 remain separate; no speculative extensibility was added.
